every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited

claims.claim: Perindoprilat, the active diacid metabolite of an ACE-inhibitor prodrug, had 30 ± 6% availability after oral perindopril in cirrhotic patients, exceeding the 20% threshold and supporting that a polar ACE-inhibitor active acid can reach F ≥ 20%.
Pidotimod, a small thiazolidine carboxylic acid with no basic center, has 42–44% oral bioavailability in humans, providing a structural analog for an ionizable thioether-proline acid exceeding 20%.
Perindopril, the ethyl ester prodrug of perindoprilat, has 66–95% absolute bioavailability in fasted humans, showing that the ACE-inhibitor scaffold is well absorbed when the acid is masked.
Ampicillin, a polar zwitterionic beta-lactam, has 29% oral absorption in fasted female subjects, above the 20% threshold.
Maraviroc has a population F of 0.24 under fasted conditions, above the 20% threshold.

evidence_gaps: No direct oral bioavailability or IV-comparison measurement for the query molecule itself.
The most relevant ACE-inhibitor context (C13) measures perindoprilat availability after oral prodrug, not direct oral administration of the active acid.
First-pass thiol metabolism (e.g., S-methylation, disulfide formation) and possible transporter-mediated absorption are not directly assessed.
Condition mismatch: query has no reported external condition; several reference contexts are cirrhosis or fasted.
content.decision_summary: Predicted high (F ≥ 20%) because all transferable reference contexts show F above threshold, with the closest analogs (perindoprilat 30 ± 6%, pidotimod 42–44%) clearly exceeding 20%, and no affirmative evidence supports F < 20%; uncertainty from indirect transfer and unfavorable logD is reflected in moderate confidence.
